<section class="ac-item-body" id="measuring-financial-stress-under-the-gold-standard-evidence-from-interwar-czechoslovakia">
<h3>Measuring Financial Stress under the Gold Standard: Evidence from Interwar Czechoslovakia</h3>
<p>A financial-only stress index and a broader macro-financial index reconstruct the monthly Czechoslovak Depression, November 1929–August 1938. The revised framework separates financial pressure from real distress and examines the February 1934 institutional break.</p>
<p><a class="pill-link" href="czechoslovakia-financial-stress.html">Dataset, findings and figures</a> <a class="pill-link" href="https://www.openicpsr.org/openicpsr/project/247312/version/V1/view">Original openICPSR V1 deposit</a></p>
</section>

<div class="ac-publication">
<section class="ac-item-body" id="missing-j-paper">
<h3>The Missing J in Interwar Europe: A Monthly Cliometric Dataset on Effective Exchange Rates and Trade-Balance Adjustment, 1925–1936</h3>
<p>Monthly evidence from eighteen European economies traces a rapid, temporary improvement in export values relative to import values after real effective depreciation. The average first-year path differs from the canonical J-curve, while historical devaluation episodes vary sharply across countries.</p>
<p class="ac-item-meta">The CSE conference version, dated 20 August 2026, develops the common-sample comparisons and small-cluster inference checks.</p>
<p><a class="pill-link" href="the-missing-j.html">Dataset, findings and figures</a><a class="pill-link" href="the-missing-j.html#citation">Versions and citation</a></p>
</section>
